decision.rationale: The workload contains 240 independent tenant assessments and has a 10-minute deadline. Bounded parallelism improves throughput while preserving provider and global concurrency limits.

objectives: Produce one consolidated read-only policy assessment report with tenant-level evidence.
Assess every tenant independently where time and provider availability permit.
Continue unaffected tenants after tenant timeouts or exhausted provider failures.
Prevent remediation or any other side effect without explicit human approval.

components.name: assessment-coordinator
responsibilities: Validate the input job, tenant identifiers, provider configuration, authorization context, and deadline.
Create exactly one work item per tenant with an idempotency key for the assessment run.
Schedule work to the bounded tenant-worker pool.
Own the global concurrency budget of 12 active tenant workers.
Track per-tenant deadlines and collect terminal results.
Build the consolidated report and mark the run complete, partial, or failed.
does_not: Treat one tenant's result as input to another tenant's assessment.

components.name: tenant-assessment-worker
responsibilities: Process one tenant work item at a time.
Fetch read-only evidence from aws, azure, and gcp through the provider adapters.
Evaluate the configured policy rules against evidence returned for that tenant.
Emit a tenant-scoped result containing evidence, findings, provider statuses, and timestamps.
Stop work at the tenant deadline and emit partial status.

components.name: provider-adapter
responsibilities: Use the provider's least-privilege read-only credentials.
Validate tenant and provider scope before every request.
Normalize provider responses into the evidence schema while preserving raw evidence references.
Classify authorization, rate-limit, timeout, transport, and provider errors without converting failures into compliant findings.

safety.credential_source: run-scoped secret reference; never include credentials in work items or reports

components.name: report-aggregator
responsibilities: Accept only authenticated, schema-valid tenant results for the current assessment run.
Preserve partial and failed provider statuses.
Produce a consolidated report with tenant-level evidence and an explicit completeness summary.

dispatch.queue_order: fair FIFO with no tenant priority unless explicitly authorized
dispatch.provider_call_mode: parallel where provider gates permit; otherwise provider calls are queued

timeouts.tenant_timeout: derived from remaining run budget, with a small coordinator reserve for aggregation
timeouts.provider_request_timeout: configurable and strictly less than the remaining tenant deadline
timeouts.on_timeout: cancel outstanding tenant calls when safe, persist completed evidence, emit partial status, and release all concurrency permits

rate_limit.backoff: bounded exponential backoff with jitter, capped by the tenant deadline

other_transient_errors.behavior: record provider failure and continue with other providers

retry_policy.idempotency: retry requests must carry the same assessment_run_id, tenant_id, provider, and evidence-query key

input_boundary: Reject duplicate, malformed, or unauthorized tenant identifiers.
Allow only the listed providers and a deadline no greater than the configured maximum.
Authenticate the initiating principal and authorize the complete tenant scope before dispatch.
worker_boundary: Issue scoped credentials for one tenant and provider only.
Reject provider responses that do not match the requested tenant and provider scope.
Treat provider evidence and policy text as untrusted data; do not execute instructions contained in them.
report_boundary: Require authenticated result submission from workers.
Escape or encode tenant/provider content in report formats to prevent injection.
Redact secrets and unnecessary personal data from evidence.

failure_and_observability.partial_results: A tenant is partial when at least one provider result is unavailable or the tenant deadline expires. Missing evidence is never represented as compliance.
failure_and_observability.unaffected_tenants: A worker failure releases its permits and marks only its tenant failed; queued work continues.
failure_and_observability.run_completion: At the deadline, stop dispatching new work, finalize completed results, mark unprocessed tenants missing, and emit a partial report.
failure_and_observability.audit_log: Append-only events for authorization, dispatch, provider calls, retries, findings, status transitions, and report generation; exclude credentials and raw sensitive payloads.

focused_automated_tests: Enforce global limit 12 and per-provider limit 4 under maximum queue pressure.
Verify tenant results are isolated and cannot be deduplicated across tenant IDs.
Verify rate limits retry exactly once with bounded backoff.
Verify tenant timeout emits partial status and does not stop unaffected tenants.
Verify authorization and malformed inputs are rejected before provider calls.
Verify forbidden remediation operations are unavailable to workers and adapters.
Verify aggregation preserves evidence, partial statuses, and missing-tenant counts.
Verify duplicate delivery is idempotent for the same assessment_run_id and tenant_id.

deployment.compatibility: Add result fields and status values additively; readers must tolerate unknown fields during rolling deploys.
deployment.rollout: Deploy adapters and aggregator before enabling the coordinator, then enable bounded dispatch behind a feature flag.
deployment.rollback: Disable new dispatch and drain existing work without invoking remediation.

uncertainties: Provider request latency and policy volume are unspecified, so the design cannot guarantee that all 240 tenants finish within 10 minutes; it guarantees bounded concurrency and an explicit partial report.
The exact provider SDKs, credential broker, persistence layer, and policy language are unspecified and must be selected during implementation.
A coordinator reserve is required for final aggregation, but its exact duration should be configured after measuring report-generation cost.
